summary: Core authorization and immutable grading pass 36 emulator tests, including explicitly enrolled anonymous browser sessions. Anonymous enrollment requires trusted-admin active:true and allowAnonymous:true, plus per-assignment grants; no new student login is required. Live deployment remains approval-gated.

findings.issue: Legacy anonymous submissions preserve prior behavior and do not prove durable student identity; Canada Test 2 questions remain statically public.
findings.recommendation: Use explicit trusted-admin enrollment and per-assignment grants for new protected content. Anonymous browser credentials persist only in that browser; a replacement browser/device needs a newly approved enrollment. Keep Canada Test 2’s existing public compatibility exception.

findings.issue: Rules intentionally accept bounded opaque response JSON; malformed direct writes can corrupt only the student-authored work for that attempt. They are detected before rendering and do not affect grading authority.
findings.recommendation: Keep revalidation and text-only rendering in every consumer; a future trusted validation backend may reject malformed JSON before storage.
